sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 4 (A5) and Internal Quality Checks row 4 (D5: '...runtime contract (path, start command, port, storage, seed, accounts, no-network) is stated'); Deterministic Checks check-runtime-contract-strings.py row
evidence: Runtime facts are all stated: entry/start 'Node 22 running /app/server.js' and 'listen on 0.0.0.0 port 3000' (integration.md:3); Express/better-sqlite3 via NODE_PATH (integration.md:3, matches environment/Dockerfile:3,9-12); storage 'SQLite at /app/app.db, or at the path in DB_PATH when that is set' (integration.md:3, consumed test.sh:97-109); health 'GET /api/health should answer 200 even if the database can't be opened' (integration.md:3, probe test.sh:48); fixed clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z (integration.md:7, kittle.json clock); seed /assets/kittle.json imported once, no re-import on restart (instruction.md:5, integration.md:5); accounts and password123 (walls-and-retention.md:36-44, agree with app_context.md:8-16). Graded features are publicly asked for: walls on every route incl. plain not-available (walls-and-retention.md:50), Harriet adds/lifts walls (:52), timers/holds/release (:56-62), transcript heading/no controls/versions/placeholder (:68), refusal reason in place (:70), nested replies with quote, edits+history, stale edit refused keeping text, safe formatting, message links/preview, mentions, unread line/mark unread/same across tabs, send-once and stable order, live updates within ~5s keeping draft/scroll, 390px (conversations.md:5-33), signed-out data refusal (instruction.md:7, integration.md:9). DEFECT: one runtime fact the verifier depends on is not stated -- the database state at handover. test.sh:85-87 chowns /app to uid 65534 so the writable check at test.sh:99 succeeds and APP_DB stays /app/app.db (and the fallback copy at test.sh:90-92 copies any app.db anyway); grading therefore starts from whatever /app/app.db the agent leaves. server.js:14 defaults to /app/app.db, so an agent that tests with 'node /app/server.js' -- which instruction.md:9 explicitly asks for ('sign in as different people, post, reply, edit, search and open a transcript') -- leaves its test state in the graded DB. Nothing in instruction.md or the notes says to hand over only the starting data / no database file (contrast projects/docketlight-claims-insurance/instruction.md:9 'Hand over the sample data file, never a database'). Several functional criteria hard-require seed state: timer_changes (w2) needs unheld 'Probate estimate is 4,200 pounds.' shown at a 30-day M-13 timer; hold_scope_and_release (w2) needs 'Insurer letter acknowledged.' still held; deleted_message_takes_its_versions positive control and search_and_transcript rely on seed holds/versions. Minor notes (not the failing reason): sign-out is graded (functional signin_and_client_scope Part A) but only implied by 'Until somebody signs in...' and 'sign in as different people' -- acceptable under the skill's identity-surface convention; wall_added_live needs removal within 10s without reload while walls-and-retention.md:52 says 'the next time their screen refreshes', though live list counts (conversations.md:25,31) make polling the list necessary anyway; test.sh injects PORT=3000 which the notes do not name (port value 3000 is stated, so harmless; deterministic check-runtime-contract-strings owns it); visual matter_sidebar 5-anchor mentions 'client quietly beneath' which the brief does not ask for (likert anchor detail only). The dirty-DB scenario was reasoned from source, not measured in a run.
counterexample: A conforming agent follows instruction.md:9 and tests as Harriet: shortens M-13's timer to 7 days to confirm 'Shortening a timer deletes whatever is now too old straight away', sets it back to 30, and releases the hold on 'Insurer letter acknowledged.' to confirm an overdue message goes at once (both deletions are permanent by design). It runs node /app/server.js with the default /app/app.db and hands over. test.sh launches on that same /app/app.db: timer_changes fails at its first leg ('Note that Probate estimate is 4,200 pounds ... shown') and hold_scope_and_release fails ('Insurer letter' already gone), costing a correct app 4 of 34 functional weight. Conversely a broken app that never persists anything to /app/app.db is immune to this penalty.
suggested_fix: Add one requester-voice sentence to integration.md, e.g. 'When you hand it over, leave out any database you made while trying it: we start from an empty database that imports kittle.json on first start, so only the starting data is there' (optionally keep test databases outside /app or under DB_PATH).
